description:
## Why

When using the Maildir backend, notmuch can index the article store. This issue wires notmuch's tag and search capabilities into stoa's JMAP layer, replacing or supplementing the Tantivy full-text search index and the UserFlagsStore with notmuch's Xapian index.

Result: JMAP Email/query text filters and keyword filters are answered by notmuch queries. JMAP keyword changes (mark seen, flag, etc.) are written back to notmuch tags. Users get a single source of truth for tags that both stoa and their notmuch MUA see.

## What

### Keyword sync (JMAP keywords ↔ notmuch tags)

Defined mapping:
- `$seen` ↔ notmuch tag absent (notmuch convention: unread = tag:unread present; seen = tag:unread absent)
- `$answered` ↔ notmuch tag `replied`
- `$flagged` ↔ notmuch tag `flagged`
- `$draft` ↔ notmuch tag `draft`
- All other JMAP keywords ↔ notmuch tags of the same name

Maildir flags in the filename (:2,RS suffix) are kept in sync with notmuch tags for MUA compatibility.

On JMAP `Email/set` keyword update: call `notmuch tag` (via subprocess or notmuch library) to apply the delta.
On read: call `notmuch search --output=tags` for the message to populate JMAP keywords.

### Search integration (JMAP Email/query ↔ notmuch query)

Map JMAP EmailFilterCondition fields to notmuch query syntax:
- `text` → bare notmuch term search
- `from` → `from:value`
- `to` → `to:value`
- `subject` → `subject:value`
- `hasKeyword` → `tag:value`
- `notKeyword` → `not tag:value`
- `before` / `after` → `date:..value` / `date:value..`
- `inMailbox` → `folder:groupname`

Unmapped filter conditions fall back to the existing Tantivy index or return empty results with a flag indicating partial results.

### notmuch invocation

Option A: subprocess (`notmuch search`, `notmuch tag`, `notmuch new`) — simple, adds notmuch as a runtime dependency.
Option B: notmuch C library via FFI — faster, no subprocess overhead, more complex.

Start with Option A (subprocess). Gate behind a `notmuch` Cargo feature.

## Dependencies

Requires stoa-hgfmg (Maildir block store backend) — notmuch integration only makes sense when articles are stored as Maildir files.

## Acceptance

- JMAP Email/query with text filter is answered by notmuch search
- JMAP Email/set keyword update is reflected in notmuch tags and vice versa
- notmuch new run after article ingest makes articles visible to notmuch MUAs
- Feature is gated behind a notmuch Cargo feature flag
- Integration tests run only when notmuch binary is present on PATH
notes: The notmuch unread convention (unread tag present = unseen) is the inverse of JMAP $seen. This is the most likely source of bugs — test it explicitly.
title: Notmuch tag and search integration
